claim: Inferring adequate kinetic schemes for ion channel gating from ensemble currents is a daunting task due to limited information in the data.
source: Inferring adequate kinetic schemes for ion channel gating from ensemble currents is a daunting task due to limited information in the data.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a motivation for the work.

claim: The generalized Kalman filter outperforms both a classical Kalman filter and a rate equation approach when applied to patch-clamp data exhibiting realistic open-channel noise.
source: Our generalized Kalman filter outperforms both a classical Kalman filter and a rate equation approach when applied to patch-clamp data exhibiting realistic open-channel noise.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 3 and 11.

claim: The derived generalization enables inclusion of orthogonal fluorescence data, making unidentifiable parameters identifiable and increasing the accuracy of the parameter estimates by an order of magnitude.
source: The derived generalization also enables inclusion of orthogonal fluorescence data, making unidentifiable parameters identifiable and increasing the accuracy of the parameter estimates by an order of magnitude.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 4 and 10.

claim: The Bayesian filter yields a realistic uncertainty quantification in contrast to the rate equation approach.
source: By using Bayesian highest credibility volumes, we found that our approach, in contrast to the rate equation approach, yields a realistic uncertainty quantification.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The Bayesian filter delivers negligibly biased estimates for a wider range of data quality.
source: Furthermore, the Bayesian filter delivers negligibly biased estimates for a wider range of data quality.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 8, 9, 11, and 12.

claim: For some data sets, the Bayesian filter identifies more parameters than the rate equation approach.
source: For some data sets, it identifies more parameters than the rate equation approach.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 7.

claim: The Bayesian filter is more robust against errors induced by analog filtering before analog-to-digital conversion than a rate equation approach.
source: Finally, we show that our Bayesian filter is more robust against errors induced by either analog filtering before analog-to-digital conversion or by limited time resolution of fluorescence data than a rate equation approach.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 11.

claim: The Bayesian filter is more robust against errors induced by limited time resolution of fluorescence data than a rate equation approach.
source: Finally, we show that our Bayesian filter is more robust against errors induced by either analog filtering before analog-to-digital conversion or by limited time resolution of fluorescence data than a rate equation approach.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 12.

claim: Disturbance of ion channel function by mutations often causes severe diseases, such as epilepsy, sudden cardiac death, or sick sinus syndrome.
source: Disturbance of their function by mutations often causes severe diseases, such as epilepsy (Oyrer et al., 2018; Goldschen-Ohm et al., 2010), sudden cardiac death (Clancy and Rudy, 2001), or sick sinus syndrome (Verkerk and Wilders, 2014) indicating a medical need (Goldschen-Ohm et al., 2010) to gain further insight into the biophysics of ion channels.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The use of Bayesian statistics in HMM estimation constitutes a major advantage.
source: It is becoming increasingly clear that the use of Bayesian statistics in HMM estimation constitutes a major advantage (Ball et al., 1999; De Gunst et al., 2001; Rosales et al., 2001; Rosales, 2004; Gin et al., 2009; Siekmann et al., 2012; Siekmann et al., 2011; Hines et al., 2015; Sgouralis and Pressé, 2017b; Sgouralis and Pressé, 2017a; Kinz-Thompson and Gonzalez, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Simultaneous orthogonal fluorescence measurement of conformational changes or ligand binding has increased insight into the complexity of channel activation in ensemble patches.
source: In ensemble patches, simultaneous orthogonal fluorescence measurement of either conformational changes (Zheng and Zagotta, 2000; Taraska and Zagotta, 2007; Taraska et al., 2009; Bruening-Wright et al., 2007; Kalstrup and Blunck, 2013; Kalstrup and Blunck, 2018; Wulf and Pless, 2018) or ligand binding itself (Biskup et al., 2007; Kusch et al., 2010; Kusch et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2011) has increased insight into the complexity of channel activation.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: A Bayesian estimator that can collect information from cross-correlations and time correlations inherent in multi-dimensional signals of ensembles of ion channels is currently missing.
source: Currently, a Bayesian estimator that can collect information from cross-correlations and time correlations inherent in multi-dimensional signals of ensembles of ion channels is still missing.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in the literature that motivates the current work.

claim: The RE approach is based on a deterministic differential equation derived by averaging the chemical master equation for the underlying kinetic scheme.
source: The RE approach is based on a deterministic differential equation derived by averaging the chemical master equation (CME) for the underlying kinetic scheme (Kurtz, 1972; Van Kampen, 1992; Jahnke and Huisinga, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Deterministic approaches do not use the information of the time- and cross-correlations of the intrinsic noise.
source: Nevertheless, all deterministic approaches do not use the information of the time- and cross-correlations of the intrinsic noise.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of deterministic approaches.

claim: Deterministic approaches are asymptotically valid for an infinite number of channels.
source: These deterministic approaches are asymptotically valid for an infinite number of channels.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical property of deterministic approaches.

claim: A time trace with a finite number of channels contains, strictly speaking, only one independent data point for deterministic approaches.
source: Thus, a time trace with a finite number of channels contains, strictly speaking, only one independent data point.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the asymptotic validity of deterministic approaches.

claim: Previous rigorous attempts to incorporate the autocorrelation of the intrinsic noise of current data into the estimation suffer from cubic computational complexity in the amount of data points.
source: Previous rigorous attempts to incorporate the autocorrelation of the intrinsic noise of current data into the estimation (Celentano and Hawkes, 2004) suffer from cubic computational complexity (Stepanyuk et al., 2011) in the amount of data points, rendering the algorithm non-optimal or even impractical for a Bayesian analysis of larger data set.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Under certain conditions, Stepanyuk's algorithm can be faster than the Kalman filter.
source: Under certain conditions, Stepanyuk's algorithm can be faster than the Kalman filter (Moffatt, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The algorithm by Milescu et al., 2005 achieves its superior computation time efficiency at the cost of ignoring the time correlations of the fluctuations.
source: The algorithm by Milescu et al., 2005 achieves its superior computation time efficiency at the cost of ignoring the time correlations of the fluctuations.
evidence: This is stated as a trade-off in the algorithm by Milescu et al., 2005.

claim: The KF is the minimal variance filter.
source: A further argument for our approach, independent of the Bayesian context, is investigated in this paper: The KF is the minimal variance filter (Anderson and Moore, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: A complete HMM analysis (forward algorithm) would deliver the most exact likelihood of macroscopic data.
source: On the one hand, a complete HMM analysis (forward algorithm) would deliver the most exact likelihood of macroscopic data.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical property of the forward algorithm.

claim: The computational complexity of the forward algorithm limits this type of analysis in ensemble patches to no more than a few hundred channels per time trace.
source: On the other hand, the computational complexity of the forward algorithm limits this type of analysis in ensemble patches to no more than a few hundred channels per time trace (Moffatt, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The authors approximate the solution of the CME with a Kalman filter to tame the computational complexity.
source: To tame the computational complexity (Jahnke and Huisinga, 2007), we approximate the solution of the CME with a Kalman filter (KF), thereby remaining in a stochastic framework Kalman, 1960.
evidence: This is stated as the methodological approach of the paper.

claim: For linear (first or pseudo) Gaussian system dynamics, the KF is optimal in producing a minimal prediction error for the mean state.
source: Notably, for linear (first or pseudo) Gaussian system dynamics, the KF is optimal in producing a minimal prediction error for the mean state.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical property of the KF.

claim: KFs have been used previously in several protein expression studies which also demonstrate the connection of the KF to the linear noise approximation.
source: KFs have been used previously in several protein expression studies which also demonstrate the connection of the KF to the linear noise approximation (Komorowski et al., 2009; Finkenstädt et al., 2013; Fearnhead et al., 2014; Folia and Rattray, 2018; Calderazzo et al., 2019; Gopalakrishnan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The authors' approach generalizes the work of Moffatt, 2007 by including state-dependent fluctuations such as open-channel noise and Poisson noise in additional fluorescence data.
source: Our approach generalizes the work of Moffatt, 2007 by including state-dependent fluctuations such as open-channel noise and Poisson noise in additional fluorescence data.
evidence: This is stated as a key contribution of the paper.

claim: Due to the state-dependent noise the central Bayesian update equation loses its analytical solution.
source: A central technical difficulty which we solved is that due to the state-dependent noise the central Bayesian update equation loses its analytical solution.
evidence: This is stated as a technical challenge addressed in the paper.

claim: The authors derived an approximation which is correct for the first two moments of the probability distributions.
source: We derived an approximation which is correct for the first two moments of the probability distributions.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological contribution of the paper.

claim: Even with simulated data of unrealistic high numbers of channels per patch (more than several thousands within one patch), the KF outperforms the deterministic approach in estimating the model parameters.
source: However, even with simulated data of unrealistic high numbers of channels per patch (more than several thousands within one patch), the KF outperforms the deterministic approach in estimating the model parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a finding of the paper and supported by data in Figure 3c.

claim: Moffatt, 2007 already demonstrated the advantage of the KF to learn absolute rates from time traces at equilibrium.
source: Moffatt, 2007 already demonstrated the advantage of the KF to learn absolute rates from time traces at equilibrium.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Stochastic models are formulated within the framework of Bayesian statistics where parameters are assigned uncertainties by treating them as random variables.
source: To select models and to identify parameters, stochastic models are formulated within the framework of Bayesian statistics where parameters are assigned uncertainties by treating them as random variables (Hines, 2015; Ball, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Previous work on ensemble currents combined the KF only with ML estimation.
source: In contrast, previous work on ensemble currents combined the KF only with ML estimation (Moffatt, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Difficulties in treating simple stochastic models by ML approaches in combination with the KF justify the computational burden of Bayesian statistics.
source: Difficulties in treating simple stochastic models by ML approaches in combination with the KF (Auger-Méthé et al., 2016), especially with non-observable dynamics, justify the computational burden of Bayesian statistics.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Bayesian statistics has an intuitive way to incorporate soft or hard constrains from diverse sources of prior information.
source: Bayesian statistics has an intuitive way to incorporate soft or hard constrains from diverse sources of prior information.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of Bayesian statistics.

claim: The Bayesian approach is still applicable in situations where parameters are not identifiable or posteriors are non-Gaussian, whereas ML fitting ceases to be valid.
source: First, the Bayesian approach is still applicable in situations where parameters are not identifiable (Hines et al., 2014; Middendorf and Aldrich, 2017b) or posteriors are non-Gaussian, whereas ML fitting ceases to be valid (Calderhead et al., 2013; Watanabe, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: A Bayesian approach provides superior model selection tools for singular models such as HMMs or KFs.
source: Second, a Bayesian approach provides superior model selection tools for singular models such as HMMs or KFs Gelman et al. (2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Bayesian statistics has a correct uncertainty quantification based on the data and the prior for the statistical problem.
source: Third, Bayesian statistics has a correct uncertainty quantification (Gillespie and Golightly, 2012) based on the data and the prior for the statistical problem.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: ML or maximum posterior approaches lack uncertainty quantification based on one data set.
source: In contrast, ML or maximum posterior approaches lack uncertainty quantification based on one data set (Joshi et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The study focuses on the effects on the posterior due to formulating the likelihood via a KF instead of an RE approach and the benefits of adding a second dimension of observation.
source: This study focuses on the effects on the posterior due to formulating the likelihood via a KF instead of an RE approach and the benefits of adding a second dimension of observation.
evidence: This is stated as the focus of the study.

claim: The study considers the performance of the algorithm against the gold standards in four different aspects: (I) The relative distance of the posterior to the true values, (II) the uncertainty quantification, (III) parameter identifiability, and (IV) robustness against typical misspecifications of the likelihood.
source: We consider the performance of our algorithm against the gold standards in four different aspects: (I) The relative distance of the posterior to the true values, (II) the uncertainty quantification, here in the form of the shape of the posterior, (III) parameter identifiability, and (IV) robustness against typical misspecifications of the likelihood (such as ignoring that currents are filtered or that the integration time of fluorescence data points is finite) of real experimental data.
evidence: This is stated as the evaluation framework of the study.

claim: The exemplary ligand-gated channel has two ligand binding steps and one open-closed isomerization described by an HMM.
source: Here we treat an exemplary ligand-gated channel with two ligand binding steps and one open-closed isomerization described by an HMM (see Figure 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: For this model, confocal patch-clamp fluorometry (cPCF) data were simulated: time courses of ligand binding and channel current upon concentration jumps were generated.
source: For this model, confocal patch-clamp fluorometry (cPCF) data were simulated: time courses of ligand binding and channel current upon concentration jumps were generated (see Appendix 5 and Materials and methods section).
evidence: This is stated as the data generation method.

claim: The KF is a Bayesian filter, that is a continuous state HMM with a multivariate normal transition probability.
source: The KF is a Bayesian filter (see Materials and methods), that is a continuous state HMM with a multivariate normal transition probability Ghahramani, 1997 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by a citation and Figure 2a.

claim: If the system strictly obeys Equation 3 and Equation 4 then the KF is optimal in the sense that it is the minimum variance filter of that system.
source: If the system strictly obeys Equation 3 and Equation 4 then the KF is optimal in the sense that it is the minimum variance filter of that system Anderson and Moore, 2012.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: If the distributions of ν and ω are not normal, the KF is still the minimum variance filter in the class of all linear filters but there might be better non-linear filters.
source: If the distributions of ν and ω are not normal, the KF is still the minimum variance filter in the class of all linear filters but there might be better non-linear filters.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical property of the KF.

claim: Below or even inside the interval Nch∈[10^1,10^2] there are more qualified concepts such as the forward algorithm or even particle filters which avoid the normal approximation.
source: Below or even inside this interval there are more qualified concepts such as the forward algorithm or even particle filters (Golightly and Wilkinson, 2011; Gillespie and Golightly, 2012) which avoid the normal approximation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The KF has a time complexity that is linear in the number of data points, allowing a fast algorithm.
source: Due to the recursiveness of its equations, the KF has a time complexity that is linear in the number of data points, allowing a fast algorithm.
evidence: This is stated as a computational property of the KF.

claim: The state-dependent noise makes the integration of the denominator of Equation 8 (which is also the incremental likelihood) intractable.
source: To the best of our knowledge such a state-dependent noise makes the integration of the denominator of Equation 8 (which is also the incremental likelihood) intractable
evidence: This is stated as a technical challenge.

claim: By applying the theorem of total variance decomposition, the authors deduce a normal approximation to Equation 8 and to the related problem of Poisson-distributed noise in fluorescence data.
source: However, by applying the theorem of total variance decomposition Equation 46a we deduce a normal approximation to Equation 8 and to the related problem of Poisson-distributed noise in fluorescence Equation 57, Equation 55a data.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological contribution.

claim: The derived equations for the covariance matrix are still exact for the more general noise model.
source: Note, that the derived equations for the covariance matrix are still exact for the more general noise model.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the derived equations.

claim: Mean and covariance just do not form a set of sufficient statistics anymore for the generalized noise model.
source: Mean and covariance just do not form a set of sufficient statistics anymore.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the generalized noise model.

claim: The derivation is not limited to ligand-gated ion channels.
source: Our derivation is not limited to ligand-gated ion channels.
evidence: This is stated as a generalization of the method.

claim: The algorithm uses automatic differentiation of the statistical model to sample from the posterior via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC).
source: Our algorithm uses automatic differentiation of the statistical model to sample from the posterior (Appendix 1—figure 1a) via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) (Betancourt, 2017), see Appendix 7 , as provided by the Stan software (Hoffman and Gelman, 2014; Gelman et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as the computational method and supported by citations.

claim: The posteriors show that both former algorithms (RE and classical KF) are further away from the true parameter values with their maxima or mean values.
source: The resulting posteriors (Figure 3a) show that both former algorithms are further away from the true parameter values with their maxima or mean values (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3a.

claim: For maximum likelihood inferences the true value would be far outside the estimated confidence interval for the RE approach.
source: Accordingly, for maximum likelihood inferences the true value would be far outside the estimated confidence interval.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the posterior distributions.

claim: The KF is more robust towards analog filtering, as the results alter less with fcut (given a reasonable fcut), and less biased for unfiltered data in the estimates of these parameters.
source: The KF is more robust towards analog filtering, as the results alter less with fcut (given a reasonable fcut), and less biased for unfiltered data in the estimates of these parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from Figure 11c.

claim: Both algorithms incur very similar bias due to the finite integration time.
source: Both algorithms incur very similar bias due to the finite integration time (Figure 12b).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 12b.

claim: The robustness of both algorithms against the cut-off frequency is compared with the robustness against the integration frequency found to be about an order of magnitude higher.
source: Based on the Euclidean error (Figures 11a and 12a) the robustness of both algorithms against the cut-off frequency is compared with the robustness against the integration frequency found to be about an order of magnitude higher.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from Figures 11a and 12a.

claim: The authors generalized the filter equations of the KF for analyzing the gating and binding dynamics of ligand-gated ion channels with a realistic signal-generating model for isolated patch-clamp (PC) and confocal patch-clamp fluorometry (cPCF) data including open-channel noise, photon-counting noise and background noise.
source: We generalized the filter equations (Methods Equation 37, 38d, 57, 58 and 59) of the KF for analyzing the gating and binding dynamics of ligand-gated ion channels with a realistic signal-generating model for isolated patch-clamp (PC) and confocal patch-clamp fluorometry (cPCF) data including open-channel noise, photon-counting noise and background noise.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the methodological contribution.

claim: The approach is derived by approximating the chemical master equation of a first order chemical reaction network which is exact up to the second statistical moment.
source: Our approach is derived by approximating the chemical master equation of a first order chemical reaction network (which ion channel experiments usually are) which is exact up to the second statistical moment.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the method.

claim: For first-order chemical reaction networks, the linear noise approximation are exact up to the second moment too.
source: For first-order chemical reaction networks, the linear noise approximation (Wallace et al., 2012) are exact up to the second moment too (Grima, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The authors' approach is equivalent to approaches based on the chemical Langevin or Fokker-Planck equations.
source: Thus, we can conclude that our Bayesian filter uses a time integrated version of the linear noise approximation. To our understanding of Wallace et al., 2012 our approach is thus equivalent to approaches based on the chemical Langevin or Fokker-Planck equations (Gillespie, 2002).
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on citations to published literature.

claim: The common assumption that for large ensembles of ion channels simpler deterministic modeling by RE approaches is on par with stochastic modeling, such as a KF, is wrong in terms of Euclidean error and uncertainty quantification.
source: With our algorithm, we demonstrate (Figures 3c and 7) that the common assumption that for large ensembles of ion channels simpler deterministic modeling by RE approaches is on par with stochastic modeling, such as a KF, is wrong in terms of Euclidean error and uncertainty quantification (Figures 5a–c ,–6a–b).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion and supported by data in multiple figures.

claim: In the other regime of lower channel expression, enriching the data by the second observable, makes non-identified parameters to identified parameters.
source: In the other regime of lower channel expression, enriching the data by the second observable, makes non-identified parameters to identified parameters.
evidence: This is stated as a finding.

claim: The second observable in cPCF data decreases the overfitting tendency of the RE approach on the true process.
source: The second observable in cPCF data decreases the overfitting tendency (Figure 4a, b and d) of the RE approach on the true process.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by data in Figure 4a, b and d.

claim: The posterior sampled by a RE approach never covers the true values within a reasonable HDCV for various signal-to-noise ratios.
source: We show for various signal-to-noise ratios (Figures 5a–c ,–6a–b) that the posterior sampled by a RE approach never covers the true values within a reasonable HDCV.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by data in Figures 5a–c and 6a–b.

claim: The central feature of Bayesian statistics, exact uncertainty quantification by having the full posterior, is meaningless in combination with an RE approach.
source: Thus, the central feature of Bayesian statistics, exact uncertainty quantification by having the full posterior, is meaningless in combination with an RE approach (considering the type of data and set of signal-to-noise ratios that we tested).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the findings.

claim: If HDCVs based on an RE approach cannot be trusted, the same applies to confidence volumes based on the curvature of the likelihood.
source: If HDCVs based on an RE approach cannot be trusted, the same applies to confidence volumes based on the curvature of the likelihood.
evidence: This is stated as an inference.

claim: The KF delivers properly shaped posteriors.
source: This is not the case for the KF which delivers properly shaped posteriors (Figures 6a–c ,–5a–c).
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by data in Figures 6a–c and 5a–c.

claim: Increasing the model complexity, at unchanged PC data quality shows that the RE approach displays unidentified rates even for large ion channel ensembles while the authors' approach identified all parameters for the same data.
source: Increasing the model complexity, at unchanged PC data quality (Figure 7) shows that the RE approach displays unidentified rates even for large ion channel ensembles while our approach identified all parameters for the same data.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: The overall superior robustness of the KF against errors of analog filtering compared to the RE approach was investigated.
source: We also investigated the robustness of both algorithms against the cut-off frequency of a Bessel filter (Figure 11) and showed the overall superior robustness of the KF against errors of analog filtering compared to the RE approach.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by data in Figure 11.

claim: One should let the KF sample as fast as possible, with a cut-off frequency of at least one order of magnitude higher than the sampling frequency of the KF.
source: Thus, one should let the KF sample as fast as possible, with a cut-off frequency of at least one order of magnitude higher than the sampling frequency of the KF.
evidence: This is stated as a practical recommendation based on the findings.

claim: The KF is more robust than the RE approach against errors due to the finite integration time.
source: Similar to the Bessel filter, the KF is more robust than the RE approach against errors due to the finite integration time.
evidence: This is stated as a finding.

claim: It is crucial for both algorithms that the intrinsic time scales (1/eigenvalues) of the process to be analyzed are slower than the integration time of the data points.
source: Nevertheless, it is crucial for both algorithms (Figure 12), that the intrinsic time scales (1/eigenvalues) of the process to be analyzed are slower than the integration time of the data points.
evidence: This is stated as a finding and supported by data in Figure 12.

claim: The approach can approximate any other stochastic system and signal distributions of linear (pseudo-first-order) kinetics.
source: Nevertheless, our approach can approximate any other stochastic system and signal distributions of linear (pseudo-first-order) kinetics (Sorenson and Alspach, 1971).
evidence: This is stated as a generalization of the method and supported by a citation.

claim: Prospective extensions of the Bayesian filter, for example by Bayesian Gaussian sum filters or similar numerically brute force concepts such as particle filters, can overcome modeling errors at low ion channel numbers or low photon fluxes.
source: Prospective extensions of the Bayesian filter, for example by Bayesian Gaussian sum filters or similar numerically brute force concepts such as particle filters (Golightly and Wilkinson, 2011; Gillespie and Golightly, 2012), can overcome modeling errors at low ion channel numbers or low photon fluxes.
evidence: This is stated as a future direction and supported by citations.

claim: State simulations were performed with 10 kHz or 100 kHz sampling.
source: Simulations were performed with 10 kHz or 100 kHz (for Figures 11 and 12) sampling, KF analysis frequency fana for cPCF data is in the range of (200-500) Hz while pure current data is analyzed at 2-5 kHz.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: KF analysis frequency fana for cPCF data is in the range of (200-500) Hz while pure current data is analyzed at 2-5 kHz.
source: Simulations were performed with 10 kHz or 100 kHz (for Figures 11 and 12) sampling, KF analysis frequency fana for cPCF data is in the range of (200-500) Hz while pure current data is analyzed at 2-5 kHz.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The Markov state model consists of two binding steps and one opening step.
source: The Markov state model (kinetic scheme) consists of two binding steps and one opening step.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The KF is a special class of models in the family of Bayesian filters.
source: The KF is a special class of models in the family of Bayesian filters (Ghahramani, 1997), which is a generalisation of the classical KF.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The KF is particularly useful for modeling time series data of ensembles dynamics of first order chemical networks due to its linear time evolution.
source: Due to its linear time evolution (Equation 1), the KF is particularly useful for modeling time series data of ensembles dynamics of first order chemical networks.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the KF.

claim: The Bayesian framework has various properties which makes it superior to ML estimation.
source: The Bayesian framework (as demonstrated in this article) has various properties which makes it superior to ML estimation (MLE) (McElreath, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Models with a hidden structure are called singular.
source: Models with a hidden structure are called singular.
evidence: This is stated as a definition.

claim: Singularity means that the Fisher information matrix of a model is not invertible leading to the breakdown of the Cramer-Rao Bound theorem.
source: Singularity means that the Fisher information matrix of a model is not invertible leading to the breakdown of the Cramer-Rao Bound theorem.
evidence: This is stated as a definition and consequence of singularity.

claim: Due to the breakdown of the Cramer-Rao Bound theorem, it cannot be guaranteed that even in the asymptotic limit the log-likelihood function can be approximated by a quadratic form.
source: Due to the breakdown, it cannot be guaranteed that even in the asymptotic limit the log-likelihood function can be approximated by a quadratic form Watanabe, 2007.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Usually the MLE does not obey Equation 22 for singular models.
source: Thus, usually the MLE does not obey Equation 22.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of singularity.

claim: The posterior distribution is usually not a normal distribution for singular models.
source: Consequently, the posterior distribution is usually not a normal distribution either (Watanabe, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Using the full posterior distribution without further approximations detects the resulting problems such as deviation from normality or non-identifiability of parameters, related to the singularity.
source: Using the full posterior distribution without further approximations detects the resulting problems such as deviation from normality or non-identifiability of parameters, related to the singularity.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of using the full posterior.

claim: The posterior is still a valid representation of parameter plausibility while ML fails for singular models.
source: In conclusion, the posterior is still a valid representation of parameter plausibility while ML fails.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the advantage of Bayesian methods for singular models.

claim: At a time, a channel can only be in a single state.
source: At a time, a channel can only be in a single state.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the Markov model.

claim: Analytical equations for the ensemble evolution that can be quickly evaluated on a computer millions of times are indispensable for Bayesian sampling.
source: Therefore, analytical equations for the ensemble evolution that can be quickly evaluated on a computer millions of times are indispensable.
evidence: This is stated as a practical requirement for Bayesian sampling.

claim: A normal distribution is the conjugated prior of the mean of a normal likelihood, but it is not the conjugated prior for the variance.
source: While a normal distribution is the conjugated prior of the mean of a normal likelihood, it is not the conjugated prior for the variance.
evidence: This is stated as a mathematical property.

claim: The derived equations for the covariance matrix are still exact for the more general noise model, but mean and covariance just do not form a set of sufficient statistics anymore.
source: Note, that the derived equations for the covariance matrix are still exact for the more general noise model. Mean and covariance just do not form a set of sufficient statistics anymore.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the derived equations.

claim: Microscopic-reversibility was applied by a hierarchical prior distribution.
source: We applied microscopic-reversibility (Colquhoun et al., 2004) by a hierarchical prior distribution.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach and supported by a citation.

claim: The hierarchical prior allows at maximum a ±0.005 relative deviation from the strict microscopic-reversibility.
source: we derived a conditional prior which allows at maximum a ±0.005 relative deviation from the strict microscopic-reversibility.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the hierarchical prior used in the study.
